cf.title: psql: Fix REPACK index completion after a column list

input.subject: [PATCH] psql: Fix REPACK index completion after a column list

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible example in message #1, the fix is confined to psql tab completion for an existing command, and it adds no syntax, GUC, catalog state or server code. The remaining points are small questions about completion behaviour, not design objections. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and nobody has replied to v3.

brief.title: psql: fix REPACK tab completion around USING INDEX
brief.problem: With a column list, psql completes `REPACK (ANALYZE) tab1 (c1) USING INDEX` with indexes from unrelated tables. The completion code takes `prev3_wd` as the table name, but that word is the column list, so the table query returns nothing and completion falls back to all indexes. The patch also merges a fix for completing INDEX after a typed `USING`.
brief.proposed_design: v3 skips the column list to find the target table when it completes an index name. It also completes INDEX after an explicitly typed USING, with or without command options or a column list. It adds no completion directly after a column list, and no column-list continuations when the command has no option list, because those forms cannot enable ANALYZE.
user_visible_surface: psql tab completion: `REPACK ... (cols) USING INDEX <Tab>` offers indexes of the named table only.
psql tab completion: `REPACK ... USING <Tab>` completes INDEX, also with options or a column list.
author_claims: Without a command option list, column-list forms cannot enable ANALYZE and are always invalid, so completing them is wrong.
Checking whether the option list enables ANALYZE adds enough complexity to justify a separate patch.
brief.thread_state: Chao Li reviewed v1 and v2 and found that v2 completed `USING INDEX` after `repack t (a)`, which the server rejects without ANALYZE. Sho posted v3 with that completion removed, and nobody has replied to v3 yet.
unclear: Whether v3 offers any completion for `REPACK (ANALYZE) t (a) <Tab>`, or leaves it as it was before the patch.
Whether an option list that does not enable ANALYZE, such as `(VERBOSE)`, still gets column-list completions in v3.
Whether this needs a backpatch, given which release first shipped REPACK.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which words and index names psql offers for REPACK in src/bin/psql/tab-complete.in.c.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, and the thread does not say which release first shipped REPACK.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds word-position rules for REPACK that must follow any later change to the REPACK grammar.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: With v3, does `REPACK (VERBOSE) t (a) USING INDEX <Tab>` still offer index names, although the server rejects a column list without ANALYZE?
What does v3 offer for `REPACK (ANALYZE) t (a) <Tab>`: the same as before the patch, or nothing?
Which release first shipped REPACK, and do you ask for a backpatch to it?
Does the table lookup still find the table when the column list has several columns or spaces, such as `(c1, c2)`?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows psql tab completion and the REPACK grammar would have to own it. No committer is visible in the thread; the only reviewer is Chao Li.
committability.liability: Low: the owner signs for a few completion rules in tab-complete.in.c and their TAP tests, which must be kept in step with the REPACK grammar.
committability.author_follow_up: Good sign: the author posted v2 and v3 within days of each review and withdrew the sibling entry #7610 as agreed in message #3.

priority.reason: The fix helps psql users who type REPACK with a column list or a typed USING. The two patches are under 3 KB each, touch one psql source file and one TAP test, and add no new user-visible surface beyond completion.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the word-position matching in v3 could not be checked against multi-column lists, schema-qualified table names or option lists without ANALYZE. Messages #4 and #5 were not shown in full.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for SELECT in psql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion after SELECT, suggesting column names from all visible tables and function names. Functions that are unlikely to be called directly are filtered out, and later versions use per-server-version queries and add completion after commas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas found the completions both too broad and too narrow: system catalog columns flood short prefixes, the FROM clause is ignored, and system columns appear inconsistently. He held that the completion must be smarter to be acceptable. He also reported that the query on pg_attribute took about 1 second on a database with a 1000-partition table. An earlier review by Peter Eisentraut found broken older-version queries and an unsettled function filter. The rebased patch of 2018-09-22 got no visible reply before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the completion needs to be smarter to be acceptable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab-completion refactoring and word-removal feature (was IF-NOT_EXISTS for tab-completion)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set refactors psql_completion by moving the macros to a new header and turning the long else-if chain into standalone ifs in a separate function. On top of that it adds word-shift and word-removal macros, keyword case that follows input, and suggestions for IF (NOT) EXISTS, OR REPLACE and other syntax.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers judged the refactoring too large and not worth the trouble so soon after the 9.6 rewrite of tab completion; Tom Lane's objection about back-patching appears only in quoted lines. Michael Paquier proposed a localized way to add IF (NOT) EXISTS through words_after_create. The author said removing the else chain is the core of the patch, so a localized patch means abandoning it, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The general consensus seems to be that this feature is too large
a rewrite of tab completion considering a major rewrite was done for 9.6.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix psql-completion for CREATE INDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes several psql tab-completion bugs: a wrong word position in ALL IN TABLESPACE OWNED BY, the misplaced CONCURRENTLY in CREATE INDEX, and a missing NULL in the SECURITY LABEL list. Later versions add IF NOT EXISTS completion for CREATE INDEX and fix DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, with an optional multilevel matching variant.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The parts were fixed or committed separately, so nothing was left to apply. The CREATE INDEX fix was done in another thread, and Peter Eisentraut committed a reduced DROP INDEX patch without IF NOT EXISTS, because psql has no IF NOT EXISTS completion elsewhere. The author confirmed the commit and said he would post IF (NOT) EXISTS support as a separate patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that we could use completion support for DROP INDEX
CONCURRENTLY, but I would rather not throw IF NOT EXISTS into the same
patch.  We don't have support for IF NOT EXISTS anywhere else.

precedents_retrieved.title: IF (NOT) EXISTS in psql-completion
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Pavel Stehule, Michael Paquier, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend psql tab completion to suggest IF (NOT) EXISTS and similar optional words, by adding a mechanism to shift the starting index of word matching and to remove optional words from the previous-words list so later matching ignores them. The later version reorganized this into a patch set that split psql_completion into a separate function, made suggested keywords follow the input letter case, added the word shift/removal feature, and added IF (NOT) EXISTS suggestions as a proof of concept.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After the patch set was reorganized, reviewers reported remaining problems: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS completion did not work, "not exists" was not offered after "create table if", there were whitespace errors, and the new macros were insufficiently documented. Michael Paquier also noted that the infrastructure changes were large for the goal of adding IF [NOT] EXISTS. The patch was not updated for over a week before the CommitFest ended, so it was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch hasn't been updated in over a week and we're just about out
of time for this CommitFest, so I've marked it "Returned with
Feedback" for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: Add tab-complete for optional view parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for the optional view parameters (check_option, security_barrier, security_invoker) in CREATE VIEW ... WITH ( and in ALTER VIEW ... SET/RESET (. A later version also completes the values of check_option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found that "alter view <name> set<tab>" does not complete to "SET (", because the "SET SCHEMA" and "SET (" choices share the prefix "SET " and no branch handles it. Dean Rasheed also objected to offering check_option in CREATE VIEW, since it steers users away from the SQL-standard WITH CHECK OPTION syntax. The author did not post a new version after the January review, and the entry was closed as stale.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: set schema" and "set (" alternatives are competing, while completion of the common part "set<space>" leads to a string composition which does not have the check branch (Matches("ALTER", "VIEW", MatchAny, "SET")).

precedents_retrieved.title: remove VersionedQuery support from psql tab completion
precedents_retrieved.summary: Remove the VersionedQuery infrastructure from psql tab completion, because it served only publications and subscriptions. After psql's minimum supported server version was raised to v10, nothing used it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that future catalog changes may again affect tab completion. SchemaQuery, the alternative, is harder to use. Nathan Bossart replied that he was fine with leaving the code in place, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Do you think we'll never again
make any catalog changes that affect tab completion?

precedents_retrieved.title: Multi-column list partitioning
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds multi-column list partitioning, so that `partition by list (a, b)` takes partitions defined by value tuples such as `for values in (1, 2), (1, 5)`. It changes bound transformation, the bound data structures, tuple routing, partition pruning, NULL handling and, in a split second patch, partition-wise join.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amul Sul questioned the pruning design. Range partitioning needs a prefix of the partition keys, but list partitions could also be pruned on later keys alone, and he judged the NULL handling in pruning to be wrong. Julien Rouhaud set the entry to Waiting on Author because of these concerns and a clang warning. The visible messages show no new patch or author reply before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I haven't studied the whole partition pruning code and don't know the complete code flow, but AFAICU, this is not the correct way to handle null value.

precedents_retrieved.title: Table AM modifications to accept column projection lists
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the table AM API so that sequential scans, index scans, tuple_lock and tuple fetch take a column projection set, so that columnar AMs such as Zedstore read only the columns a query needs. The planner and executor collect these sets, for example scanCols and returningCols in RangeTblEntry, with separate sets for RETURNING, EPQ checks and ON CONFLICT UPDATE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The authors withdrew the patch. They said it was hard to review in its current form and that no concrete implementation of the new API existed in core, and they had no time to improve it before the July commitfest. Reviewers had raised smaller points, such as adding scan_begin_with_column_projection as a new callback instead of extending scan_begin, but nobody objected to the design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We agree that
it's fairly difficult to review in its current state, and the lack of a
concrete implementation of the new API isn't helping.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
Reverted commit(s): Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables; Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables; Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables; autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables; Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned tables on ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts the following commits:
1b5617eb844cd2470a334c1d2eec66cf9b39c41a Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables
0e69f705cc1a3df273b38c9883fb5765991e04fe Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables
41badeaba8beee7648ebe7923a41c04f1f3cb302 Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables
0827e8af70f4653ba17ed773f123a60eadd9f9c9 autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables

There are efficiency issues in this code when handling databases with
large numbers of partitions, and it doesn't look like there isn't any
trivial way to handle those.  There are some other issues as well.  It's
now too late in the cycle for nontrivial fixes, so we'll have to let
Postgres 14 users continue to manually deal with ANALYZE their
partitioned tables, and hopefully we can fix the issues for Postgres 15.

I kept [most of] be280cdad298 ("Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned
tables on ANALYZE") because while we added it due to 0827e8af70f4, it is
a good bugfix in its own right, since it affects manual analyze as well
as autovacuum-induced analyze, and there's no reason to revert it.

I retained the addition of relkind 'p' to tables included by
pg_stat_user_tables, because reverting that would require a catversion
bump.
Also, in pg14 only, I keep a struct member that was added to
PgStat_TabStatEntry to avoid breaking compatibility with existing stat
files.

Backpatch to 14.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] is a different set of psql completion fixes, and its reason (keep IF NOT EXISTS out of the same patch) does not apply, because the reviewer in message #2 asked for the two related REPACK fixes to be merged. [P11] and [P18] cover COPY option completion and record no reason. The thread cites only the withdrawn sibling entry from message #3, which this patch absorbs.

From the standards and compatibility angle this is a small psql tab-completion fix. It adds no syntax, no GUC, no catalog state and no dump output, and existing scripts behave the same. Completing INDEX after USING follows the existing CLUSTER pattern. v3 leaves completion directly after a column list unchanged, which settles the issue from message #4. One inconsistency is left: v3 can still look up indexes after an option list without ANALYZE, such as `(VERBOSE)`, which the server rejects. psql completion is best-effort elsewhere too, so this is not worth an objection. Whether a backpatch is needed depends on the release that first shipped REPACK, which the material does not say.

The patch changes only psql tab completion in tab-complete.in.c and its TAP test. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol message or extension API, so nothing persistent or cross-node is affected. Backpatching would not be limited by ABI.

The patch has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes which index names psql tab completion offers for REPACK, and those names come from catalog queries that the connected user can already run. It adds no new privilege, default, server code path or data exposure.

From the maintenance angle there is no objection. The patch is a small fix in tab-complete.in.c, built on the same word-position matching that the existing completion rules use. It adds no hot-path cost, no API and no new mechanism, and it comes with TAP tests. The open point is the deferred check for whether the option list enables ANALYZE, and that is a later improvement. Nobody has reviewed v3 yet, and no committer has joined the thread.

This is a bug fix to existing psql tab completion for REPACK, and no existing feature, extension or tool offers the corrected completion. Tab completion lives only in psql's tab-complete.in.c, so this angle has no in-core or out-of-core alternative to name.

This is a small bug fix to existing psql tab completion for REPACK, a command that already ships. Completing indexes from unrelated tables is wrong behaviour that any REPACK user can hit, so it does not need separate evidence of demand. The fix touches only tab-complete.in.c and its TAP test, and adds no UI, GUC or hot-path cost for anyone else.
